Subject: SIG upload constraints and preferred workflow

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for partnering with us on the SIG. Our procurement portal has two constraints that matter for uploads: single-file max = 25MB, and the portal prefers PDF uploads (no nested zips). We also have a hard requirement to receive a clear evidence index mapping each questionnaire answer to supporting docs.

Question: can you deliver the SIG in incremental chunks (questionnaire first, then evidence bundles) over the portal, or do you prefer a staged S3 handoff we can pull from? Also, do you have a recommended naming convention and a checksum file we can use to validate files after upload?

We aim to start ingesting on Tuesday 4/20 and would like to schedule a one-hour window to avoid partial ingestion.

Thanks,
Linda

Hi Linda — thanks for the details. Confirmed we can do incremental delivery; below is our proposed upload plan and QA checklist.

Plan (high level):
- Deliverable A (Day 0): "SIG_Questionnaire_vRedwood_YYYYMMDD.pdf" — exported flattened PDF of the completed SIG answers (searchable).
- Deliverable B (Day 0+): Controls Appendix + short control narratives as a separate PDF: "SIG_Controls_Appendix_vRedwood_YYYYMMDD.pdf" (keeps questionnaire smaller).
- Deliverable C (staged, bulk within 48 hours): Evidence bundle split into per-control chunks, each <= 24MB, named: "SIG_EVID_<controlID>_<shortdesc>_v1.pdf".
- Accompanying files: evidence_index.csv (maps questionID -> filename -> page ranges), checksums.sha256, and a short manifest.txt with MD5/size metadata.

Portal vs S3: We can upload directly to your portal if it accepts incremental files (recommended) OR we can place a staged, time-limited S3 folder and share links for your procurement team to ingest. For large evidence sets we prefer the S3 staging flow (faster, resumable).

PDF preparation rules (QA checklist):
- Flatten/linearize PDFs (no embedded multimedia or bookmarks).
- Remove internal-only comments and redactions applied where necessary.
- Add a single page header on each evidence PDF: "Redwood Inference — SIG Evidence — filename" with generation timestamp.
- Include a signed manifest page in the first PDF of each bundle: author, date produced, sha256 manifest name.
- Do not combine > 24MB per file to keep portal-friendly.

Attachments included: SIG_packaging_plan_draft.pdf (outline + sample filenames), evidence_index_v1.csv, checksums.sha256 (sample).

Open questions for you:
1) Is your portal OK with files named using underscores?
2) Can procurement confirm if a staging S3 link is acceptable as an alternative?
3) Do you require a separate notarized cover letter or is the manifest page sufficient?

Marissa / Rishi — looping you in for any additional constraints (PDF stamping, legal redlines, or SOC2 references).

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Manager, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Vanessa — nice outline. A couple practical tweaks based on recent uploads to marketplace portals: 

- Remove PDF bookmarks/outlines; procurement portals sometimes preserve bookmarks and that causes indexing errors.
- Use PDF/A when possible for the questionnaire export (improves long-term fidelity).
- Evidence PDFs: avoid OCR overlays that create duplicate text layers — we prefer clean OCR or native text.
- For the evidence_index.csv please include these columns: question_id, filename, page_start, page_end, redaction_flag (yes/no), source_system. This helps their intake team map quickly.
- For checksums.sha256 use the canonical filename + space + hash format so the portal can verify with standard tools.

One more operational note: when we do incremental uploads, include a small "ready-for-ingest" marker file in S3 (ready.txt) with the manifest checksum. Procurement can poll for that file as the signal to begin ingestion.

If procurement will use the portal, confirm the maximum files-per-batch they allow; we'll throttle accordingly.

Marissa
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
